title: Platform systems & services: runbooks, alerts, dashboards, roadmap (Q4 2026)
author: Anika Patel
content:
Overview

This document is the canonical team playbook for Platform Systems & Services (PSS). It consolidates runbooks, monitoring thresholds, dashboard ownership, alerting policies, short-term roadmap items, and a short retrospective summary for Q3 - Q4 2026. The goal is to provide clear, actionable guidance for oncall, SRE, and platform engineers responsible for keeping Redwood's inference platform available, performant, and cost-efficient.

Scope

- Services covered: platform-api, ingress-proxy, model-routing, batch-scheduler, kv-cache, metrics-ingest, autoscaler-controller, infra-operator.
- Environments: prod (global), staging, canary.
- Audience: oncall SREs, platform engineers, support, and engineering managers.

Key contacts and ownership

- Platform SRE lead: Marcus Nguyen (primary escalation)
- Platform runtime owner: Priya Singh
- Observability & dashboards: Diego Morales
- Pager: #platform-oncall (Slack), oncall rotation in PagerDuty: PSS-primary -> PSS-secondary

Section 1 - SLOs and error budgets

Primary availability SLOs (prod):

- platform-api: 99.95% availability (monthly) - target latency p95 < 120ms, p99 < 250ms for 512-token requests
- ingest-proxy: 99.9% availability (monthly) - p95 < 50ms
- model-routing (inference control plane): 99.9% availability - p99 tail latency for routing decisions < 50ms

Error budget burn thresholds and actions:

1. < 25% monthly error budget used: normal operations.
2. 25% - 75% used: notify product and pause non-essential rollouts.
3. > 75% used: require incident review and rollback any recent infra changes (see rollback checklist).

Section 2 - Dashboards & ownership

Canonical dashboards (Grafana):

- Platform Overview (dash id: 3142) - owner: Diego Morales - shows global traffic, request rate, 5xx rate, cost per token estimate.
- Model Routing Health (dash id: 3157) - owner: Priya Singh - routing latency, route failures, fallback rate by model variant.
- Autoscaler & Capacity (dash id: 3201) - owner: Capacity team - GPU utilization, pending pods, scale events.
- Ingest & Metrics (dash id: 3308) - owner: Observability - scrape success, ingestion lag, prometheus remote write errors.

Dashboard maintenance rules:

- Dashboards must include: last data time, owner label, and a link to runbook.
- Every dashboard has a monthly ownership review: confirm metrics and thresholds are still valid.

Section 3 - Alerts and thresholds

Alerting principles:

- Prefer SLO-based alerts (error budget burn) before raw symptom alerts.
- Use multi-step alerting: Warning -> Critical -> Page. Warnings go to #platform-monitoring, Critical pages PSS-primary.
- Keep alerts actionable: each alert must include: symptom, likely causes, first 3 diagnostic steps, and runbook link.

Representative alert rules (Prometheus-style, simplified):

1) platform_api_high_5xx
- Expr: increase(platform_api_http_requests_total{status=~"5.."}[5m]) > 0.5
- Severity: critical
- Pager: PSS-primary
- Runbook: section "Runbook: platform-api 5xx"

2) platform_api_latency_p99
- Expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(platform_api_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le)) > 0.25
- Severity: warning (>=3x baseline)

3) prometheus_remote_write_failures
- Expr: rate(prometheus_remote_write_err_total[5m]) > 0
- Severity: warning

Alert noise mitigation checklist:

- Deduplicate alerts with routing labels (region, cluster).
- Suppress low-volume noisy alerts during deploy windows using the deploy tag.
- For high-cardinality metrics, aggregate by service and origin before alerting.

Section 4 - Runbooks (quick actionable steps)

Runbook: platform-api 5xx (pager triggers)

1) First responder (oncall): Acknowledge the PagerDuty incident.
2) Primary checks (5 minutes):
   - Confirm scope: is it all regions or single region? (Grafana -> Platform Overview).
   - Check recent deploys: gitops commit window, and /deployments in cluster.
   - Check error type: auth errors vs upstream model errors. Use: 
     - kubectl -n platform logs deploy/platform-api --since=10m | grep -i "5.." | head -n 100
   - Inspect Nginx/ingress errors: kubectl -n ingress logs daemonset/ingress-nginx --since=10m | tail -n 200
3) Mitigation (if traffic-wide 5xx):
   - If caused by faulty config or release, roll back last deploy: helm rollback platform-api <previous_release> or revert GitOps PR.
   - If due to downstream model timeouts, increase model-routing timeout (config: model-routing.timeout_ms) temporarily and enable canary fallback to lighter model.
4) If mitigation fails after 20 minutes: escalate to Platform SRE lead and open an incident command channel (#platform-incident).
5) Post-incident: file postmortem link in incident ticket within 48 hours.

Runbook: autoscaler stuck (pods pending)

1) Check pending pods: kubectl get pods --field-selector=status.phase=Pending -n inference | grep Pending
2) Check events and node resources: kubectl describe pod <pending-pod> && kubectl get nodes -o wide
3) Check cluster autoscaler logs and GPU capacity API: kubectl -n kube-system logs deploy/cluster-autoscaler
4) Quick fix: if capacity is available but scheduling fails due to taints/affinities, create a temporary toleration or scale up using capacity API: aws/gcp CLI to increase GPU pool size.

Section 5 - How-tos and common procedures

How to run a local dashboard snapshot:

- Step 1: Export query time window from Grafana: Share -> Export PNG/JSON.
- Step 2: Run preflight checks: scripts/observability/preflight.sh --target=prod --window=15m

How to perform a safe canary rollout (platform-api):

1) Create canary config (10% traffic) and schedule: gitops/apps/platform-api/canary.yaml
2) Monitor p95/p99 and 5xx for 30 minutes.
3) If metrics stable and no errors, promote to 50% for 15 minutes, then full rollout.
4) If error budget burn accelerates, abort and rollback.

Section 6 - Roadmap (next 6 months, Q4 2026 - Q1 2027)

Planned initiatives and owners:

- Observability: unified trace+metrics correlation (owner: Diego) - target: Q1 2027. Deliverable: single-pane incident view and span-to-log linking.
- Cost-efficiency: token-cost pipeline to alert on top-10 expensive prompts (owner: FinOps/Platform) - target: Q4 2026.
- Autoscaler improvements: predictive scaling using short-term workload forecasting (owner: Capacity) - target: Q1 2027.
- Runbook automation: add remediation playbooks to runbook-runner (owner: Platform) - target: Q4 2026.

Prioritization notes:

- Observability work ranks high due to incident time-to-detect regressions in Q3. Cost pipeline prioritized to help sales & customers with billing transparency.

Section 7 - Q3 retrospective (what we learned)

Summary:

- Incidents in Q3 were dominated by two classes: a) model routing regressions after a config change and b) autoscaler latency causing scheduling bottlenecks during peak nightly batch windows.
- Root causes: insufficient canary coverage for route config plus autoscaler scaling cooldowns mis-tuned for GPU warmup.

Actions taken:

- Enforce mandatory delta testing for routing config PRs with simulated traffic. (Owner: Runtime)
- Improved autoscaler configuration: added GPU warmup window and pre-warming hooks for large batch jobs. (Owner: Capacity)
- Added an SLO-based alert for rapid error budget burn. (Owner: Observability)

Section 8 - Post-incident and continuous improvement

- Each incident must result in a postmortem with a clear owner for each action item and a completion date.
- Monthly operational review: walk through top alerts, dashboard changes, and open runbook action items.

Appendix A - Useful commands and snippets

- Tail recent platform-api logs: kubectl -n platform logs -l app=platform-api --since=15m --tail=500
- Check prometheus remote write health: curl -s http://prometheus:9090/api/v1/targets | jq '.data.activeTargets[] | select(.scrapePool=="remote-write")'
- Example Prometheus alert (YAML snippet):
  - alert: PlatformHigh5xx
    expr: increase(platform_api_http_requests_total{status=~"5.."}[5m]) > 0
    for: 2m
    labels:
      severity: critical
    annotations:
      summary: "Platform API returning 5xx errors"
